Definition: from G2904; to use strength, i.e. seize or retain (literally or figuratively):--hold (by, fast), keep, lay hand (hold) on, obtain, retain, take (by).
BiblicalUsage: Krateo is the word for holding on with strength, and it covers everything from taking someone by the hand to holding fast to the truth. In Hebrews 4:14 we are told to "hold fast our profession," in 2 Thessalonians 2:15 to "hold the traditions" taught by the apostles, in John 20:23 the apostles are given power to retain sins, and in Revelation 2:13 the church at Pergamos is praised because it held fast Christ's name.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the Christian life is largely a holding: holding fast the confession, holding the traditions once delivered, and holding on to Christ Himself when the world pulls the other way. What I hold fast to holds me, and that is why I will not let go.
